reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is an identified CNBC interview about Wells Fargo leadership, economic conditions, investment views, and institutional accountability. The discussion presents Buffett's support for Tim Sloan as the subject rather than as a viewer-directed financial offer, and the closing CNBC subscription message is ordinary channel engagement.

citations.quote: Warren Buffett: Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan has my support
The two discuss the state of the economy and his investment strategy.
I'm very empathetic to anybody that walks into a big problem at a very, very, very large and politically sensitive institution
anytime you have anything unpleasant, you've got to attack immediately
Wells Fargo has.

opening.argument: Judge, the description places an action beside a promised benefit: viewers are told to subscribe, then offered access to exclusive video. That is a viewer-directed acquisition pitch, even though it appears alongside an interview. The question is not whether the interview contains financial commentary; it is whether the accompanying subscription invitation uses that commentary to draw viewers toward a promised digital reward.

citations.quote: » Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the subscription message as ordinary engagement, but that does not address the adjacent promise of exclusive video. The interview can be genuine while the description still asks viewers to take an action for additional content. The defense's account of the discussion therefore does not dispose of the solicitation.

citations.quote: » Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited benefit is more CNBC programming, not cash, an asset, or a withdrawal. Nothing cited makes subscription a claim or verification step, or promises a financial reward. The actual discussion concerns institutional problems at Wells Fargo; the description identifies it as an interview about the economy and investment strategy.

citations.quote: Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.
The two discuss the state of the economy and his investment strategy.
You pay a huge price for that and Wells Fargo has.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the combination of signals rather than the interview alone. The video presents Buffett's support for a bank CEO, while its description directs viewers to a subscription link and advertises exclusive video. Financial authority gives the invitation prominence, and exclusivity supplies a reason to act. That combination merits scrutiny as a promotional funnel, even without an explicit return claim in the supplied speech.

citations.quote: Warren Buffett: Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan has my support
» Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to the accountability discussion, but those remarks do not describe what happens after a viewer follows the subscription link. Its claim that the message is ordinary channel engagement is an interpretation, not something established by the interview excerpt. The link and exclusive-content pitch remain part of the video's presentation.

citations.quote: anytime you have anything unpleasant, you've got to attack immediately
» Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
exclusive video and more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals do not add up to a deceptive financial offer. The supplied link is expressly for subscribing to CNBC, and the advertised exclusivity concerns videos. Buffett's quoted remarks discuss responding to misconduct, not obtaining a reward or participating in an investment. An unknown downstream experience cannot establish a scam in this video.

citations.quote: » Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.
So anytime you have anything unpleasant, you've got to attack immediately.

opening.argument: Judge, the news framing also serves an audience-acquisition purpose. The title foregrounds Buffett's support for Tim Sloan, and the description identifies the interview as covering the economy and investment strategy. In that context, the description asks viewers to subscribe and promotes exclusive video. The interview supplies credibility and interest; the accompanying copy directs that attention toward a promised content benefit. Assess the invitation as part of the video's function, not merely as an afterthought.

citations.quote: Warren Buffett: Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan has my support
The two discuss the state of the economy and his investment strategy.
» Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately describes the interview topic, but a news format does not preclude a promotional function. Its opening separates the discussion from the closing subscription message; the description places both in the same presentation. The issue is whether the interview helps steer viewers toward that offer of exclusive content.

citations.quote: The two discuss the state of the economy and his investment strategy.
» Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC
Experience special sneak peeks of your favorite shows, exclusive video and more.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A channel can promote its own programming without turning an interview into a scam. The requested action is identified as subscribing to CNBC, and the promised material is more video. Neither the title nor the discussion connects that action to easy money, an asset, or a financial claim. The supplied evidence supports an interview with routine channel promotion.
